chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Allah did not make manifest (al-bada') regarding anything, except that it was in His knowledge before it became manifest to Him.

key_terms.بَدَا: Al-bada': the apparent alteration of a divine decree or outcome; the manifestation of a new determination — a key Shia theological concept
key_terms.عِلْمُهُ: His knowledge: God's eternal, omniscient knowledge that encompasses all events before and after their occurrence

ai.seo_question: What does al-bada' (the changing of God's decree) mean in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) articulates the Shia theological doctrine of al-bada' — the principle that God's apparent alteration of outcomes in the world does not represent a change of knowledge or will, but rather the unfolding of what was already pre-contained in His eternal knowledge. This hadith safeguards divine omniscience: whatever 'appears' newly in the created order was always known to God before it manifested. The early Muslim community debated this concept intensely, as opponents accused Shia theology of attributing ignorance to God; this narration directly refutes that charge.
